acceptance_criteria: A heater widget exists, is exercised by its own widget_studio tab, and renders without measurably degrading frame time.
description:
NEW WIDGET. Verified 2026-08-13: crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/components/ has NO heater.rs. Everything else on the maintainer's art list already has a starting point; this one does not.

CIET's heater is the electrically-heated test section that drives the loop. It needs to show at least: applied power, surface/fluid temperature distribution along its length, and on/off or power-setpoint state.

Build it on the NEW widget libraries, consistent with the recently-reworked components (see excursion.rs, pebble_bed_texture.rs and control_rod_drive.rs for the current house pattern, and the widget_studio example for how tabs exercise a widget in isolation).

Note the existing performance lesson before drawing anything heavy: op-szmi.12 recorded 19,874 circles per frame from shared pebble-bed artwork causing GUI lag in BOTH simulators, fixed by a texture bake. Do not re-introduce per-frame primitive floods.
title: CIET v3 art: HEATER widget — does not exist yet, new build

description:
The bed sits on a conus tapering from r=90 cm to the 25 cm discharge tube,
height 36.946 cm (Terry 2005 Fig. 2 / TECDOC-1382 Table 2), and it is FULL OF
PEBBLES. The current model is a flat-bottomed cylinder, so it omits that fuel.

The omission pushes k DOWN, i.e. toward the measured -909 +/- 108 pcm residual,
which makes it the leading named candidate for closing the remainder.

BLOCKER: needs conditional tile omission / per-tile rejection against a cone
surface. HexLattice has no such mechanism -- HEX_NONE marks only the skewed
array's unused corners. Options recorded on op-867c: a bespoke universe per
boundary tile via surface_in_tile_frame (works today, cost is one surface per
boundary tile at build time), real per-tile omission in HexLattice (cleanest,
largest change), or rejection in the delta path's material_at closure.

ZCone exists in geometry/surface.rs, so the surface itself is available.

Also unmodelled and worth listing here: the bottom is currently symmetric with
the top rather than conus + discharge tube, and the control-rod boring region
(r 95.6-108.6 cm) is solid graphite rather than homogenised with its borings.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
Conus modelled. The stated blocker (conditional tile omission) DID NOT EXIST: Geometry::locate runs find_cell (a CSG region test) before descending into a lattice, so a ZCone on the bed cell's region clips the pebble lattice for free, exactly as ins(7) already clipped it to r<90. All three recorded options rejected as unnecessary; no lattice mechanism written.

Geometry verified two ways before the eigenvalue: kernel volume +14.8 +/- 4.2 % vs +13.6 % predicted from the frustum (0.3 sigma); non-conus fraction of the sampling box 0.127070 vs 0.12707 predicted (exact); zero untiled with the filler removed.

Result: k 0.995200 +/- 0.001082 -> 1.040984 +/- 0.001148, i.e. -909 -> +3670 pcm vs RMC. Conus worth +4578 +/- 158 pcm (29 sigma). Predicted SIGN confirmed; magnitude overshoots 5x. That means the old -909 pcm was two offsetting errors. Follow-up filed. NOT COMMITTED.

title: Model the HTR-10 conus -- 36.946 cm of pebbles below the bed, needs conditional tile omission

description:
Future crate. BISHAN = **B**uilding **I**nternal **S**ource-term and **H**azard **A**nalysis **N**etwork, following the workspace MRT-station-backronym convention (cf. OUTRAM PARK, RAFFLES, FARRER PARK).

## Scope — Level 2 PSA

Level 2 probabilistic safety assessment: what happens AFTER core damage. Takes
Level 1's core-damage sequences as input and produces a source term.

- Severe-accident progression in-vessel and ex-vessel
- Containment / building response — pressure, temperature, structural challenge,
  bypass and leakage paths
- **Source-term dispersion mechanisms WITHIN the building** — the "Building
  Internal" of the name. Inter-compartment transport and mixing, aerosol
  agglomeration/settling/resuspension, plateout and revaporisation on surfaces,
  pool scrubbing, filtration and holdup along the leakage path.
- Radionuclide transport, deposition, revaporisation and retention
- Source term: release fractions by nuclide group, timing, energy
- Containment event trees / release categories binning the sequences

Level 1 (core damage frequency) and Level 3 (offsite/atmospheric consequence)
are OUT of scope for this crate, and should be recorded separately if wanted.
Note the boundary: dispersion INSIDE the building is BISHAN's; dispersion
downwind of the release point is Level 3 and is not.

## Dependencies

**Depends on `raffles` (op-vjw).** Level 2 PSA is inherently probabilistic —
the event trees, release-category binning, and uncertainty propagation come
from the UQ / risk-analysis core rather than being reimplemented here. This
resolves what was previously recorded as an open question: raffles owns the
probabilistic machinery, BISHAN owns the physics.

Also gated on the severe-accident cluster already in the tracker:

- op-4pw  melcor: DECISION — crate shape + the uom-boundary solver pattern
- op-2w6  melcor-cvh: evaluate the dwsim-libs flash as the CVH thermodynamic kernel
- op-mqj  melcor-cvh: two-phase pool+atmosphere control volume with N non-condensables
- op-52t  melcor-exec: executive, adaptive dt with step-halving, restart records
- op-acl  kovan: ingest the public MELCOR/CORCON/CONTAIN/SPARC manuals into open/

CONTAIN (containment analysis) and SPARC (pool scrubbing) are the directly
relevant upstream references for the in-building dispersion physics; CORCON
covers core-concrete interaction. op-acl should land first — the manuals are
the specification.

## Open questions, NOT decided

- Whether BISHAN is a separate crate or a module inside whatever op-4pw decides
  the MELCOR crate shape to be. op-4pw is the blocking decision.
- Upstream licence provenance for anything ported. MELCOR itself is NOT open
  source and is export-controlled — only the PUBLIC manuals are in scope per
  op-acl, and no MELCOR source may be ported. CONTAIN/SPARC availability needs
  checking before any port is planned.

## Constraints

Per RESPONSIBLE_USE.md this is for education, research and V&V only — NOT for
licensing decisions, safety-critical decision-making, emergency response, or
safeguards/security-sensitive analysis. A source-term tool is exactly the kind
of thing that must carry that framing prominently.

Filed 2026-09-14 at the maintainer's request while discussing crate naming; the
name was reserved for this before the maths-crate naming discussion.
title: BISHAN — Level 2 PSA: building internal source-term and hazard analysis

description: Port solvers/onePhase/** : porous momentum (anisotropic Kd drag + tortuosity diffusion), porous energy coupled to structure, PIMPLE pressure. First end-to-end single-phase TH run.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content: Ported solvers/onePhase: porous UEqn (isotropic Kd drag from FSDragFactor via PorousDrag+fs_drag), incompressible PIMPLE pEqn, EEqn with linearised semi-implicit structure heat source. Enum dispatch ThermalHydraulicsSolver{OnePhase}. Constant-property slice (fluid thermo pkg still scaffold). V&V (2026-07-15, isolated mirror crate, 20/20 pass): laminar Darcy Kd=32mu/Dh^2 exact; laminar spin-up terminal U=f_body/Kd exact <1e-6; turbulent Darcy-Weisbach U=sqrt(2 f_body Dh/(f0 rho)) rel<1e-5; porous energy equilibrates T->Twall <1e-4 K. clippy clean, android check clean. Files: mod.rs porous_drag.rs one_phase.rs tests.rs. Follow-up: anisotropic Kd (localX/Y/Z), onePhaseLegacy, full StructureCell field assembly.

title: genfoam TH: one-phase porous solver (UEqn/EEqn/pEqn)
